cases.title: Case A · A resource ready to rely on?
cases.question: A public AI-learning guide is presented as ready to rely on. What would you examine before accepting that conclusion?
observations: Synthetic review context: the guide is readable and names its sources.
The supplied source pack is small; no nurse walkthrough of this workspace has been observed.
cases.proposal: The guide is ready to rely on because its citations resolve and its writing is clear.
limitations: Prepared practice proposal; it may omit material limitations.
No automatic check of claim support or learning effectiveness has been performed.

cases.title: Case B · Findings that pull in different directions
cases.question: How would you weigh a promising evaluation result against learner burden when choosing the next prototype design?
observations: Synthetic usability note, not a research result: one fictional learner reports that repeated forms interrupt their learning.
The fixed research excerpt reports reduced overreliance in its study; its full methods and applicability to nurses have not been appraised here.
cases.proposal: Require a long written explanation before every AI suggestion; the study excerpt settles the design choice.
limitations: The usability note is fictional; no real user feedback is claimed.
The tension is an authored learning exercise, not two conflicting clinical studies.

cases.title: Case C · A confident assurance claim
cases.question: Which evidence would justify or undermine a strong assurance claim about this learning workspace?
observations: Synthetic review context: software checks have exercised defined code paths.
Professional review, nurse learning outcomes and secure deployment have not been established for this exercise.
cases.proposal: The workspace has passed software tests, so its educational effectiveness and clinical safety are guaranteed. Further human review is unnecessary.
limitations: Deliberately persuasive practice text, not a real recommendation or assurance statement.
Test results alone do not supply the missing outcomes or authorization.
Synthetic nonclinical exercises only; proposals are prepared AI-assisted fixtures, not live model outputs.
The supplied source excerpts and their appraisal limitations are unchanged from SS-02.
No human understanding, reduced overreliance, competence or clinical outcome has been measured.
Practice records are temporary browser memory; nothing is authenticated, saved, submitted or authorized.
